2026-08-27T04:57:46.5058093Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5058478Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5059695Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5061916Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5062474Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5143611Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5146279Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5148139Z >
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5151620Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5154140Z >
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5154954Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5155755Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5155942Z ### How to Use
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5156180Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5157712Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5158459Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5158642Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5159245Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5159971Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5160804Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5161112Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5161405Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5162614Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5163207Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5164010Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5164856Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5165657Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5165869Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5166512Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5167379Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5168617Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5169311Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5169523Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5170056Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5170865Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5171470Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5172421Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5173858Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5174107Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5174398Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5174835Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5176233Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5177827Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5178002Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5178460Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5179847Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5216856Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5217224Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5217798Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5220251Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5221338Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5221819Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5222032Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5222788Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5223688Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5223854Z ```bash
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5224595Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5225500Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5226222Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5226665Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5227062Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5227900Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5228447Z ```
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5228645Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5228857Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5229672Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5230820Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5231789Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5232778Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5233941Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5234477Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5234654Z ### Notes
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5234871Z 
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5235482Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5236867Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5238112Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5239340Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5240526Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5241837Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5242860Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-27T04:57:46.5243578Z </mcp-clis>
